title: Release window preflight + dependency impact calls
body:
Meeting: Release Window Preflight + Dependency Impact Calls
Date: 2026-03-09 (sync + async followups through 2026-03-11)
Organizer: Aisha Patel (release coordinator)
Attendees: Aisha, Miguel, Claire, Omar, Priya, SRE oncall (Ben), Platform eng rep (Jae)

Purpose / TL;DR:
- Quick preflight for the March 12 release window: validate dependency readiness, confirm rollback gates, and coordinate late-breaking hotfix call flow. Focus on cross-team handoffs (platform, serving-runtime, console) and any private/VPC customer blockers.

Agenda:
1) Quick state recap of the train + critical tickets (5m)
2) Dependency impact calls: heavy-weight infra changes + migration windows (15m)
3) Feature-flag gating and rollout plans (10m)
4) Rollback criteria + healthcheck endpoints (10m)
5) Oncall escalation path and communication cadence during the 3-hour launch window (10m)
6) Action items and owners (5m)

Notes / discussion highlights:
- Train state: most PRs merged; noted exception: PR #128 (release-orchestrator) still has integration tests failing in macrotask path. Miguel to push a hotfix branch and coordinate with release-orchestrator owner. Jira: RELEASE-412 flagged as blocker if not green by EOD 3/10.

- Dependency impact calls: we ran short 'impact' calls with Platform and SRE to confirm the infra DB migration will be done in canary subnets only. Key constraint: migration lock will run 02:00-03:00 UTC on 3/12 and requires feature flags to pin legacy auth for 30 minutes after. Platform (Jae) confirmed runbook and snapshot recovery tested in staging; recommended one additional smoke test post-migration for write-heavy endpoints. Miguel added test to the automated canary suite.

- Private deployments: Claire called out two customers in private VPCs (Cust-Alpha, Cust-Gamma) still pending endpoint cert rotation. Risk: if certs fail, rollback time is ~45 mins due to manual ops. Action: Priya to open a dedicated support channel and own preflight cert check on 3/11 morning.

- Feature flag gating: we will use the grayscale flag 'rv2-release-gf' to gate new runtime changes. Canary rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 90 minutes with automated rollback on error rate > 2.5% or p95 latency increase > 50ms. Rollback will be automated via rollback pipeline unless manual hold requested by SRE.

- Rollback criteria & health checks: agreed health suite includes:
  - /health/basic (status, DB connected)
  - /health/latency (p50/p95 token generation)
  - error-rate tracked via SLO dashboard (alerts: >1% user-visible errors in 5m window)
  - tail-latency tracing check using trace-samples tag 'release-window-3/12'
If any critical alert fires, the oncall will call the release coordinator and we flip the flag. If automated rollback fails after 3 attempts, escalate to exec oncall.

- Oncall + comms: primary oncall Ben, secondary oncall Priya (backup). Use the following channels in order: 1) slack #release-ops (pinned incident doc), 2) PagerDuty release-ops escalation, 3) conference bridge (number in confluence playbook). We will publish minute-by-minute status in a running doc and update customer success for enterprise customers at T+30/60/120 minutes.

Open risks (ranked):
- R1: RELEASE-412 test failure (blocker) — mitigation: hotfix branch + extra integration run; owner: Miguel; due: 2026-03-10 EOD
- R2: Cust-Alpha cert rotation failure — mitigation: preflight cert check and standby ops runbook; owner: Priya; due: 2026-03-11 09:00 PT
- R3: Migration snapshot restore time longer than expected — mitigation: Platform to run dry-run in staging and validate snapshot restore within 20 mins; owner: Jae; due: 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC
- R4: Automated rollback pipeline flaky on edge cases — mitigation: add one manual rollback play in runbook and test in staging; owner: Omar; due: 2026-03-11

Decisions taken:
- Proceed with release window on 2026-03-12 at 02:00 UTC assuming RELEASE-412 green by 2026-03-10 EOD.
- Use grayscale feature-gate 'rv2-release-gf' with automated rollback thresholds defined above.
- Prioritize private-customer cert checks; if either Cust-Alpha or Cust-Gamma not green, move their traffic to legacy endpoints and continue release for hosted customers only.

Action items (owner -> task -> due):
- Miguel -> Merge hotfix branch for release-orchestrator + kick extra integ run -> 2026-03-10 EOD
- Priya -> Run certificate preflight for Cust-Alpha and Cust-Gamma, create support channel -> 2026-03-11 09:00 PT
- Jae -> Run snapshot restore dry-run in staging, share timings -> 2026-03-11 18:00 UTC
- Omar -> Add manual rollback step to runbook and validate in staging -> 2026-03-11
- Claire -> Confirm private deployment runbook links and add explicit contact list for customer success -> 2026-03-10 12:00 PDT
- Aisha -> Publish minute-by-minute launch doc + schedule postmortem 3/13 10:00 PT -> 2026-03-12 14:00 UTC

Follow-ups / notes to self:
- Keep release window slack pinned messages minimal and only escalate via PD for true P0 events.
- We should capture a quick 'mini postmortem' template to speed up post-release triage (Aisha to draft).
- Consider adding a quick synthetic that simulates 5m sustained write load for the migration path next cycle.

Appendix: quick links referenced in call:
- Confluence playbook: confluence:release-window-playbook-v2
- Jira: RELEASE-412
- PR: github.com/redwood/release-orchestrator/pull/128
- SLO dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/dashboards/slo-release-window

End of notes.
